threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope, key workflows, and initial backlog for the support portal.

messages.text: Team, let's kick off the Unified Customer Support Portal project. The main goal is to get an MVP ready for pilot in 21 days. To start, let's define the absolute core features we need for the portal and knowledge base. What are your thoughts on the minimum viable scope? I've set up a sheet to track our work in A3.

Thanks for kicking this off. From the support side, the MVP must solve our biggest time sink: finding customer history and relevant KB articles. I'd propose we focus on: 1. A unified agent dashboard showing customer ticket history. 2. A searchable knowledge base integrated into that dashboard. I've started documenting the detailed agent workflows for T1 in A1.

That makes sense. Focusing on the agent dashboard first is the right call. For T2, we can create wireframes for just that core view, including the ticket list and KB search. We should also ensure the front-end for the agent dashboard, T4, is responsive from the start.
For the backend part of that, T3, we'll need access to the ticketing system's sandbox API. Do we have credentials and documentation for that yet? The integration is a key dependency.

I agree with @377231. A focused dashboard is achievable. We should also consider accessibility basics for T4, like keyboard navigation, even in the MVP. It's easier to build it in now than to add it later.

I've already requested sandbox access and I'm chasing IT for it. Should have it by EOD. So, let's lock in the MVP scope. How does this sound: Core features are 1) Agent dashboard with ticket list/search, 2) Customer details view, and 3) Integrated KB search. This seems to cover the essentials.
That list is perfect. It directly addresses the primary pain points from A1. I approve this scope for the MVP.
Works for us on the front-end. That's a clear and deliverable scope.
Great, D1 is settled. Now for ownership of the initial tasks. I propose: T1 to @6869, T2 to @377231, T3 to @109718, and T4 to @561396. Can we get drafts/initial versions done in the next 3 days?
Confirmed for T1. The draft of A1 will be ready for review tomorrow morning.
I'll take T2. I can have initial wireframes ready in 2 days.
I can take T3. I'll start as soon as we have the sandbox access.
Happy to own T4. I'll start setting up the project structure today.
Excellent. D2 is confirmed. I've updated A3 with the owners and timelines. Let's get building.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in information architecture, UX flows, and agent scripts.

messages.text: Team, I've uploaded the first draft of the wireframes and site map to A5, covering the core agent dashboard flow for T2. Please take a look and provide feedback, especially on the main navigation and information hierarchy.

Thanks @377231, this looks like a great start. The flow is clean. My main feedback is that the Knowledge Base search bar could be more prominent. It's the tool agents will use most frequently during a call. This UX directly impacts the call scripts we're drafting for T5.
That's a sharp observation. I agree, we should elevate the search bar. I can mock up an alternative with it in the main header, always visible. Give me an hour.

Looking at the 'Customer History' widget in the wireframe. What data are we planning to show there? The current ticket API only returns the last 10 tickets and limited fields. Will that be enough for the MVP?
For the MVP, the last 10 tickets should be sufficient. Let's not get blocked on extending the API. We can create a follow-up task for a more comprehensive history view post-pilot.

Thanks @561396. I've just updated A5 with a new version incorporating the more prominent search bar. With that change, I believe the overall information architecture and main navigation flows are solid. Can we get agreement on this direction?

The new version is much better, it aligns perfectly with the agent workflows documented in A1. I approve this IA. Based on this, I can finalize the list of standard call scripts for T5. I propose we create scripts for the top 5 call types: 'Password Reset', 'Billing Inquiry', 'Status Update', 'Technical Issue', and 'Product Question'.
The IA looks good and that list of scripts for T5 seems right for the pilot. I'm good with both.

Perfect. We have a decision on the IA and the script list. D3 and D4 are locked in. I'll mark T2 as complete. @6869, let us know when the draft of the scripts is available in A2. We'll need it for the front-end work on T4.
Will do. I'll have the first draft of A2 ready for review by EOD tomorrow.

threads.thread_goal: Resolve technical integration and security approach for MVP.

messages.text: Quick update on T3: I've successfully connected to the ticketing system sandbox and can search for tickets. However, the telephony system API is using a custom authentication method that's not well-documented. It might take some time to figure out. I've logged the details in A8.

Let's not let the telephony API block us. The core functionality is ticketing. I propose for the MVP we scope out the telephony integration and focus exclusively on a solid ticketing system connection. We can create a stubbed endpoint for the telephony data on the front-end for now.
I strongly agree. From an agent's perspective, seamless ticketing is 90% of the value. The CTI pop-up is a nice-to-have. Let's defer it and ensure the core workflow is flawless for the pilot.
That clarifies things for the front-end. So we will build the dashboard without the CTI pop-up for now. Thanks for the clear direction.
Ok, it's settled then. D5: MVP integration scope is ticketing system only; telephony is out. I'll update the master tracking sheet A3.

Speaking of technical decisions, I've completed the first draft of the security checklist A4 for T8. It covers the key requirements from the ICT security legislation, including authentication, authorization, and data handling. Could everyone please review it? We need to approve this as our baseline to avoid any issues close to launch.
Thanks for creating this. I've had a look at A4. It seems very thorough. The requirements for logging and error handling are clear and I can implement them as part of T3 and T6.
This is great, very clear. From a front-end perspective, we'll ensure we adhere to the guidelines on input validation and handling auth tokens.
Excellent work on this checklist, @6869. It's exactly what we need. I see no blockers here. Let's formally approve it as our go-live baseline. Any objections?
Hearing none, let's lock it in. D6: Security checklist A4 is approved. I'll mark T8 as complete. By the way, @337175, great progress on T10, the staging environment is really fast.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare and confirm the pilot plan, training, and feedback loop.

messages.text: Hi all, following up on T9, I've drafted the pilot training plan and a quick-start guide. It's based on the scripts in A2. I've also identified a pilot group of 5 experienced agents who are ready to go. Can we confirm a pilot start date of next Monday?
From the front-end side, we're on track. The KB management UI (T7) and the customer self-service pages (T11) will be feature-complete and deployed to staging by Thursday. Next Monday works for us.
The backend services are stable and deployed. Staging is ready. Monday is good for me.
I will double-check the monitoring and logging on the staging environment before the pilot starts to make sure we can catch any issues.
Perfect, thanks everyone. So we are all aligned on the pilot group and a start date of next Monday. D7 is confirmed.

Now for the feedback process during the pilot (T12). I propose we use a shared spreadsheet, A7, for logging all feedback, bugs, and suggestions. I will also run a 15-minute daily sync with the pilot agents to consolidate their thoughts. We can then review A7 as a team twice a week to prioritize.
That sounds like a great, structured process. Using A7 will be much more efficient than trying to track feedback from multiple sources. I'm all for it.
Agreed. A clear feedback loop is critical for the pilot's success. This process works.

Excellent. D8 is confirmed. I will set up the feedback log A7 and share the link shortly. As a final point, I've also drafted the Knowledge Base Content Governance Rules in A6, which defines the process for creating and maintaining articles. Please review when you have a chance.
Will do. Thanks for being so on top of all the process documents, @6869. It's a huge help.
